name: CA-28
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+14 district with entrenched incumbent Judy Chu
Chu's roughly $3.7M-to-$205K cash advantage over Verlato
Prediction markets price a ~97% Democratic win
model.rationale: The district's fourteen-point Democratic lean, Chu's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing her near-certain reelection all point the same direction, and no polling or ratings suggest anything otherwise.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a sudden influx of Republican outside spending would warrant a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 28th District, centered in the San Gabriel Valley, leans Democratic by about fourteen points on recent partisan performance. Judy Chu has held the seat since 2009 and advanced directly to the general election, while Republican April Verlato, a former Arcadia mayor, is the challenger. No public polls of the race are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and betting markets.

Chu holds a decisive financial edge, with roughly $3.7 million banked against Verlato's $205,000, and outside spending on either side is minimal. Prediction markets put her chances near 97 percent. The combination of a strongly Democratic electorate, an entrenched incumbent, and a large resource gap leaves Verlato a narrow path to an upset. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of genuine competition.
